Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

proportion noun

relation in size or amount

also in proportion, in proportion to, proportional, proportionally, proportionately, ratio, pro rata

classical

Cic. de Or. 2.320: prō portiōne rērum
Cato Agr. 106: prō portiōne ea omnia facitō (Lewis & Short)

prō portiōne

phrase: prō with the ablative of portiō

in proportion, proportionally; with a genitive, in proportion to

The classical phrase; portiō alone, “a share”, is post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). For “a large proportion of” Latin says magna pars (see most, the greater part).

Other words

  • prō ratā parte — proportionately, each by its due share

    phrase: prō with the ablative of rata pars, a fixed share · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.94: perinde ut cuique data sunt prō ratā parte; Cic. Rep. 2.67: utinam ex omnī senātū prō ratā parte esset!

    Rata pars is a fixed, reckoned share (ratus, from reor); the phrase is the source of English “pro rata”.

  • prōportiō, prōportiōnis f. — proportion, analogy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Varr. L.L. 10.2: prōportiō, quod dīcunt ἀνάλογον (Lewis & Short); Cic. Tim. 4 (Lewis & Short: Univ. 4)

    A learned word of grammar and mathematics, which Cicero offers as a new coinage for Greek analogia (Lewis & Short); in talk the phrase prō portiōne is more natural.

Examples

  • oportet, ut aedibus ac templīs vestibula et aditūs, sīc causīs prīncipia prō portiōne rērum praepōnere

    as houses and temples have forecourts and entrances, so cases should be given openings in proportion to their matterCic. de Or. 2.320

  • Omnia ista, perinde ut cuique data sunt prō ratā parte, ita aut longa aut brevia dīcuntur.

    All those things are called long or short according to the share each has been given.Cic. Tusc. 1.94

See also part, most, measure.
